title: Tokenization-aware latency buckets and SLO crediting telemetry
creator: Priya Natarajan
description:
Problem: token-level latency SLIs currently assume a 1:1 token cost and uniform tokenization across models and regions. In practice, different tokenizers and model families result in widely varying token counts for the same semantic request. This skews per-token SLI calculation, SLO burn rates, and makes cross-model/regional SLO comparisons noisy.

Goal: implement instrumentation that buckets latency by effective tokenization granularity and emits SLO-crediting metrics that normalize for tokenizer differences. This will: 1) provide accurate per-request SLO credit accounting for multi-model routes; 2) enable regional SLO policies to account for tokenizer-induced variance; 3) improve attribution when circuit breakers/firewalls trigger load-shedding by isolating tokenization effects from serving-path latency.

Scope: telemetry only (no changes to circuit-breaking behavior). Produce dashboards and a synthetic prober that exercises diverse tokenization patterns. Deliverables: metric schema, ingestion pipeline rules, Grafana/Looker dashboard buildout, prober harness, and an SLO crediting mapping document for Runtime and Console teams.
acceptance_criteria: New metrics emitted: tokenization_bucket (categorical), token_count_effective (int), token_latency_bucketed (histogram), slo_credit_weight (float)
Ingestion rules transform raw per-token measurements into normalized SLO credit events consumed by existing SLO pipeline
Dashboards show tokenization cohorts (BPE, WordPiece, char), p50/p95/p99 latencies normalized per effective token and raw token counts side-by-side
Synthetic prober runs cover at least 10 tokenization edge cases and produces reproducible golden-probe traces
Documentation: onboarding guide for product/console explaining how SLO crediting and bucketing are computed
No measurable performance regression on the ingestion path (<= 2% CPU/latency overhead) verified in staging
work_items: Design metric schema and labels (observability eng + runtime)
Implement tokenization metadata tagging in request router (route-level model tokenizer hint)
Emit per-request token_count_effective and slo_credit_weight at transport boundary
Transform pipeline: add bucketing and normalized SLO event emitter (ingest job + kinesis rule)
Build Grafana panels: cohort comparison, normalized burn rate, regional variance map
Create synthetic prober scenarios and integrate into CI canary (10 cases)
Run staging load test and measure ingestion overhead; iterate on sampling if needed
Write docs and run walk-through with Console and SRE teams
comments: 2026-02-12 Priya Natarajan: Created ticket after SRE postmortem; initial approach proposes adding slo_credit_weight derived from tokenizer characteristics and request semantics.

2026-02-18 Ethan Morales: Architecture sync with observability; decided to push tokenization hint as an optional header computed in the router to avoid touching model charcount code paths. Trade-off: some routes may not provide hints; fallback to heuristic token sampler is required.

2026-02-23 Mei Chen (Observability): Proposed three buckets for tokenization_cohort: BPE, WordPiece, Char-N; also recommended including model_family label for easier roll-ups. Mei: ensure cardinality stays low to avoid high metric cost.

2026-02-28 Design review: PMs asked for concrete examples of how SLO crediting will affect billing-facing SLOs. Decided to produce both raw and normalized SLO burn visualizations for 30-day comparison window.

2026-03-03 Dev update: router PR opened to emit X-Tokenizer-Hint and token_count_raw; initial telemetry spike observed in staging (10% increase in events). Taking sampling approach: emit full telemetry for 1% of traffic and aggregated histograms for remaining.

2026-03-06 SRE feedback: sampling must preserve p99 fidelity for tail-latency investigations. Action: implement reservoir sampler that biases towards high-latency requests and preserves all circuit-break event traces.

2026-03-09 QA: Synthetic prober run shows consistent delta between raw-count SLO burn and normalized SLO burn on en/de translations (~18% difference). Schedule a canary dashboard review with Console team on 2026-03-15.
2026-03-10 Ethan Morales: Marking in-progress tasks for ingest pipeline and dashboard. Next: finalize metric names and submit final PRs for ingest transforms.
notes_for_oncall: If synthetic prober detects >25% divergence between raw and normalized SLO burn for a region, escalate to SRE and pause automated SLO-driven throttles for that region until investigation completes.
Reservoir sampler must never drop events marked with circuit_breaker_triggered=true
